title: Correcting a Misspelled Traveller Name on an Air Ticket Fare Brands Ticket
content:
A misspelling of the traveller's name is corrected on a ticket issued under the Air Ticket Fare Brands against the fare brand's name-correction fee, provided the number of characters that differ from the identity document does not exceed the brand's character limit.

## 1. Once per booking

A name-correction line is raised only when no name-correction line has already been raised against the same booking. The test is made against the lines already standing on that booking, matched by the booking's own reference and by their being name corrections; a second line on the same booking is outside this condition.

## 2. Beyond the limit

A difference larger than the brand's character limit is not a correction but a change of traveller, which no brand permits: the ticket is cancelled on the brand's own terms and a new ticket is sold.

## 3. The authority for the correct spelling

The correction is made against the identity document held on the traveller's profile and never against what the caller says the spelling should be.

## 4. Contact details

Correcting the contact address or contact number on a booking is free on every brand and is not a name correction.

## 5. Where the fee is zero

A brand whose name-correction fee is zero still applies its character limit, because the limit is the airline's and not the agency's.

## 6. Branch table

| The difference from the identity document | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| at or within the brand's character limit, no earlier correction on the booking | corrected against the brand's name-correction fee |
| at or within the limit, a correction already raised on the booking | outside the condition in section 1 |
| larger than the brand's character limit | a change of traveller: the ticket is cancelled on the brand's own terms and a new ticket is sold |

## 7. Hypothetical boundary

On a brand whose character limit is 3, a spelling differing in exactly 3 characters is at the limit and does not exceed it, so it is corrected against the brand's fee; a spelling differing in 4 characters exceeds the limit and section 2 governs instead. On a brand whose fee is 0.00 USD the same two readings hold unchanged, since the limit applies whatever the fee.
